newsitem.title: UK: US Treasuries idle in London, await lift from data.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries idle in London, await lift from data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London idled at steady levels on Wednesday, awaiting a plethora of data to provide an excuse to push them higher, traders said.
Investors were likely to be insprired by a benign set of figures, but given the strong rally in Treasuries, they would probably be cautious in sparing more money.
Highlights of Wednesday's data are the June consumer price index (CPI) at 1230 GMT, and industrial production and capacity utilisation at 1315 GMT, expected to point to a soft economy.
"If they are benign you'll see an initial spate of buying this afternoon," said a trader in London.
"People have still got money to go to work but it's far less than it was. People are looking for an excuse to buy the market as opposed to wanting to buy it," he added.
By 0945 GMT, the 30-year bond was at 101-00 and yielding 6.54 percent, compared with 100-31 in Tokyo and 101-01 in New York. Prices were static in the shorter end.
A Reuters poll of economists forecast the CPI up 0.2 percent, industrial production up 0.2 percent and capacity use at 83.6 percent.
But Dick Howard, senior economist at Julius Baer Investments in London, said U.S. bonds were expensive unless they began to factor in rate rise, which was unlikely.
"The U.S. economy is almost perfect, the one thing that is slightly worrying is asset price inflation, which next year will become consumer price inflation," Howard said.
"I wouldn't like anywhere in the yield curve but you have more protection in the short end than the long end," he said.
Further out, the spotlight will be on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on July 22. "If there are surprises they are going to be nasty ones," said Howard.
The key thing to watch for was Greenspan's comments on the U.S. equity market, which has risen some 25 percent in the past six months.

Howard said a study comparing yields between 10-year bonds and U.S. dividends showed that the equity market was expensive compared with bonds. Economists say any correction in share prices could result in a cash influx into bonds.
Wednesday's economic data also include real earnings for June at 1400 GMT and business inventories for May at 1230 GMT.
September T-bonds were up 2/32 at 114-00 in automated trade.
